articles.summary: El calendario peruano de 2026 contempla fechas especiales durante noviembre. Conoce cuántos feriados quedan este mes, qué días se celebran y si habrá jornadas de descanso para los trabajadores del sector público y privado.
articles.body_text: Los días libres son una oportunidad para compartir tiempo en familia, organizar actividades personales o realizar pequeños viajes sin las obligaciones habituales del trabajo. En noviembre de 2026, el calendario peruano contempla fechas de descanso que deben distinguirse entre feriados nacionales y días no laborables establecidos de manera extraordinaria. Estas últimas disposiciones están vinculadas con la visita del papa León XIV al Perú y comprenden jornadas y horarios específicos en Lima, Callao y otras regiones del país. Además, no todos los trabajadores tendrán las mismas condiciones para acceder a estos descansos, pues algunas medidas requieren compensar posteriormente las horas que se dejen de trabajar. Conoce qué fechas están previstas para noviembre, en qué lugares se aplicarán y cuáles son las diferencias que debes tener en cuenta antes de organizar tus actividades. El calendario de noviembre tiene un feriado nacional, el pasado 1 de noviembre, día de todos los santos, sin embargo; también cuenta con días NO laborables según lo indica la ley. Estas últimas fueron oficializadas mediante el Decreto Supremo N.º 020-2026-TR, publicado en el diario oficial El Peruano. El calendario contempla las siguientes fechas: La compensación dependerá del sector laboral. En las entidades públicas, las horas pendientes deberán recuperarse dentro de los diez días posteriores al descanso o cuando lo determine el titular de cada institución, de acuerdo con las necesidades del servicio. En las empresas privadas, empleadores y trabajadores podrán acordar cómo reponer el tiempo no trabajado. Si no consiguen llegar a un consenso, el empleador establecerá las condiciones para realizar la compensación correspondiente. Aunque ambas fechas permiten interrumpir las actividades habituales, tienen condiciones distintas. El feriado constituye un descanso obligatorio reconocido por ley y no requiere recuperar las horas que correspondían a esa jornada. En cambio, los días no laborables suelen estar dirigidos principalmente al sector público y contemplan la recuperación posterior del tiempo pendiente. Para los trabajadores privados, su aplicación depende del acuerdo entre empleadores y trabajadores. Según la Cámara de Comercio de Lima (CCL), si un empleado trabaja en un día feriado debido a necesidades de la empresa o rotación de turnos, y no recibe un día libre en sustitución, debe recibir una compensación económica equivalente a tres veces su salario habitual por esa jornada laboral. Esto se debe a tres conceptos: No cumplir con el pago adicional o negar la compensación de descanso constituye una infracción muy grave en materia laboral. Las sanciones económicas varían según el tipo de empresa, y pueden ir desde poco más de 1.000 soles hasta superar los 24.000.

articles.title: Feriados en noviembre 2026 en Perú: ¿Cuántos feriados y días no laborables tiene?
articles.summary: El calendario peruano de 2026 contempla fechas especiales durante noviembre. Conoce cuántos feriados quedan este mes, qué días se celebran y si habrá jornadas de descanso para los trabajadores del sector público y privado.
articles.body_text: Los días libres son una oportunidad para compartir tiempo en familia, organizar actividades personales o realizar pequeños viajes sin las obligaciones habituales del trabajo. En noviembre de 2026, el calendario peruano contempla fechas de descanso que deben distinguirse entre feriados nacionales y días no laborables establecidos de manera extraordinaria. Estas últimas disposiciones están vinculadas con la visita del papa León XIV al Perú y comprenden jornadas y horarios específicos en Lima, Callao y otras regiones del país. Además, no todos los trabajadores tendrán las mismas condiciones para acceder a estos descansos, pues algunas medidas requieren compensar posteriormente las horas que se dejen de trabajar. Conoce qué fechas están previstas para noviembre, en qué lugares se aplicarán y cuáles son las diferencias que debes tener en cuenta antes de organizar tus actividades. El calendario de noviembre tiene un feriado nacional, el pasado 1 de noviembre, día de todos los santos, sin embargo; también cuenta con días NO laborables según lo indica la ley. Estas últimas fueron oficializadas mediante el Decreto Supremo N.º 020-2026-TR, publicado en el diario oficial El Peruano. El calendario contempla las siguientes fechas: La compensación dependerá del sector laboral. En las entidades públicas, las horas pendientes deberán recuperarse dentro de los diez días posteriores al descanso o cuando lo determine el titular de cada institución, de acuerdo con las necesidades del servicio. En las empresas privadas, empleadores y trabajadores podrán acordar cómo reponer el tiempo no trabajado. Si no consiguen llegar a un consenso, el empleador establecerá las condiciones para realizar la compensación correspondiente. Aunque ambas fechas permiten interrumpir las actividades habituales, tienen condiciones distintas. El feriado constituye un descanso obligatorio reconocido por ley y no requiere recuperar las horas que correspondían a esa jornada. En cambio, los días no laborables suelen estar dirigidos principalmente al sector público y contemplan la recuperación posterior del tiempo pendiente. Para los trabajadores privados, su aplicación depende del acuerdo entre empleadores y trabajadores. Según la Cámara de Comercio de Lima (CCL), si un empleado trabaja en un día feriado debido a necesidades de la empresa o rotación de turnos, y no recibe un día libre en sustitución, debe recibir una compensación económica equivalente a tres veces su salario habitual por esa jornada laboral. Esto se debe a tres conceptos: No cumplir con el pago adicional o negar la compensación de descanso constituye una infracción muy grave en materia laboral. Las sanciones económicas varían según el tipo de empresa, y pueden ir desde poco más de 1.000 soles hasta superar los 24.000.

articles.title: Piura: Senamhi advierte altas temperaturas de hasta 36°C y no descarta lluvias
articles.summary: La entidad meteorológica informó que el aumento de la temperatura estará vigente desde este lunes 9 hasta el jueves 12 de noviembre.
articles.body_text: El Servicio Nacional de Meteorología e Hidrología del Perú (Senamhi) advirtió sobre el incremento de las temperaturas en la costa norte, donde los valores podrían superar los 36 °C durante los próximos días. La alerta meteorológica estará vigente desde este lunes 9 hasta el jueves 12 de noviembre. La Dirección Zonal 1 del Senamhi precisó que el incremento de la temperatura estará acompañado de una mayor radiación ultravioleta y ráfagas de viento que podrían alcanzar velocidades cercanas a los 45 kilómetros por hora. De acuerdo con el Aviso Meteorológico Regional N.° 206 de Senamhi, las temperaturas máximas en la costa norte oscilarán entre los 23 °C y 36 °C, mientras que en la sierra norte se esperan registros de entre 19 °C y 32 °C. El pronóstico contempla tres niveles de intensidad: amarillo, por condiciones moderadas; naranja, por intensidad fuerte; y rojo, por condiciones extremas. Asimismo, la institución meteorológica señaló que no se descartan lluvias en la costa norte. La posibilidad de precipitaciones responde a las condiciones atmosféricas que se vienen registrando en la región. En otro reporte, Senamhi informó que Piura registró importantes acumulados de lluvia durante la semana pasada. La localidad de Alamor presentó el mayor registro, con 35,8 milímetros, seguido de Hacienda Barrios (18,1 mm), Partidor (13.8 mm), Paimas (10.5 mm) y El Ciruelo (7.4 mm). La entidad también reportó que el contenido de agua precipitable (PWAT) en Piura supera los 55 milímetros y alcanza valores cercanos a los 62 milímetros. Este indicador evidencia una concentración de humedad en la atmósfera, condición que puede favorecer la formación de precipitaciones cuando coincide con escenarios de inestabilidad atmosférica y ascenso del aire. Ante este panorama, se recomienda a los ciudadanos de Piura y otras localidades de la costa norte mantenerse atentos a los comunicados oficiales del Senamhi.

articles.title: Otter AI can now follow conversations across 30+ languages | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Otter AI just added support for 27 languages and revealed an upcoming feature that can follow along if speakers switch between languages.
articles.body_text: Otter.ai, the AI-powered note-taking tool, announced Tuesday that it’s expanding its multilingual capabilities, including a new multilingual transcription feature that can follow conversations as speakers switch between languages during the same meeting. The company is also adding support for 27 languages, its largest language expansion to date. Once the rollout is complete, Otter will support 31 languages in total, making the platform more accessible to international teams. The upcoming feature will automatically detect language changes and continue transcribing without requiring users to adjust settings. For example, a call could move from English to Korean to Portuguese, with Otter following the conversation throughout. The update aims to address a common challenge for global teams, where language differences can make meetings and collaboration more difficult. “Otter is breaking down language barriers so any company, no matter where they’re based, can build a system of record for the decisions for voice AI communication,” an Otter spokesperson told TechCrunch. Thirteen of the new languages are available now: Mandarin Chinese, Korean, German, Italian, Cantonese, Portuguese, Russian, Indonesian, Malay, Dutch, Turkish, Vietnamese, and Polish. The remaining 14 languages are coming soon and include Swedish, Danish, Finnish, Arabic, Hindi, Thai, Hebrew, Norwegian, Greek, Macedonian, Persian, Czech, Hungarian, and Romanian. The newly added languages run on Otter’s own speech models. The company told us it trained them using publicly available datasets and worked with native-speaking volunteers to review transcripts and check accuracy. The announcement comes as Otter continues to expand beyond transcription and into other workplace AI tools, following its $320 million funding from General Catalyst. It recently introduced Work Mode, which uses meeting history and connected apps to help users prepare for upcoming calls. For instance, the feature pulls information from previous customer conversations, outstanding action items, notes from teammates’ similar calls, and recent Google Drive files. Another recent addition is Live Assist, which provides real-time coaching during meetings. It analyzes the conversation and offers relevant suggestions based on what has already been talked about and what is happening in the moment. articles.title: California's proposed 'billionaire tax' fails to pass | TechCrunch
articles.summary: California voters rejected Proposition 40, the one-time 5% tax on billionaires, the AP reported Monday. Tech leaders outspent backers roughly 10 to 1 to defeat it, and the founders and economists TechCrunch interviewed before the vote were split on whether it would have driven out wealthy residents or just trimmed their fortunes.
articles.body_text: California voters have rejected Proposition 40, the state’s proposed one-time tax on billionaires, the Associated Press reported Monday . The measure failed after an expensive campaign that pitted labor unions against some of tech’s wealthiest figures. It was also opposed by Gov. Gavin Newsom. Nic Carter lives about as far from Silicon Valley as you can get within the continental U.S. but his feelings about California’s proposed tax on billionaires couldn’t have been stronger. Carter, a Floridian, and a general partner at the crypto-focused venture capital firm Castle Island Ventures, told TechCrunch before the vote that he thought the proposal — it was on the ballot during California’s midterm election last week — would actually have been a huge win for more fiscally conservative states like his own. “I think it’d be it would be great for Florida and Texas if these kinds of taxes pass,” Carter said last week. “I think it’s a shame, frankly, that California has this sort of semi-monopoly on capital formation, and that it’s being squandered by local governance that’s super dysfunctional.” Proposition 40, otherwise known as the California “billionaire’s tax,” was a ballot measure that proposed the creation of a special one-time 5% wealth tax to be levied against state residents with a net worth of more than $1 billion. The tax, which would have been applied retroactively to anyone who was residing in California on January 1, 2026, would have been used to fund a number of public programs — most notably Medi-Cal, the state’s Medicaid program that provides healthcare to qualifying low-income residents. Proponents of the proposal — largely labor unions — said it would have inconvenienced a tiny number of state residents, as California has a little over 200 billionaires who own a cumulative total of approximately $2 trillion in wealth. In return, they said, it would generate massive amounts of revenue. Its backers projected it could have raised as much as $100 billion over five years, the likes of which could then have been used to support public healthcare and education. But opponents argued that it would scare California’s wealthiest residents out of the state and ultimately disincentivize growth. The capital flight argument — that California’s upper crust would permanently flee, thus draining a more consistent source of revenue for the state — dominated conversations online among business leaders in the run-up to the vote. A critical but contested analysis published before the vote claimed the proposal would actually have lost the state money over time. “You’re signaling to the entrepreneur class that you consider them a resource to be plundered,” he said. Carter, who frequently works in San Francisco with tech startups, claimed such a tax would “inhibit venture capital investment” because VCs “wouldn’t necessarily want to invest in a company if they knew the founder was going to have to liquidate a huge percentage of their shares.” The logic: since many billionaires keep a majority of their wealth tied to their companies, it would be inconvenient for newly minted billionaires to make liquid a certain percentage of that wealth just so that they could pay the tax. Jesse Tinsely, a California entrepreneur who has spent his life working in startups, agreed. Tinsely is the co-founder and CEO of Mainstreet, a fintech holding company that owns employment sites like Employer.com and Recruiter.com. Tinsely founded his first startup many years ago and said that, based on his own experience, what he had accomplished wouldn’t have been possible with the proposed tax. Additionally, he reiterated a widely held fear — that founders, who could be taxed on their corporate assets, would be incentivized to give up control over their companies. “I bootstrapped my business. I have super voting shares, and I came from a [background as a] college dropout [and] broke firefighter with bad credit and whatnot, and built a business that’s valued into the billions,” Tinsely said last week. “I think it [the tax] removes the ability to do something like that.” Tinsely said he felt the proposed tax “forces founders to opt into a system” where “anyone who wants to become an entrepreneur has to…raise money or some type of capital, or move. Those are basically the only two options.”

articles.title: Jensen Huang's alleged honeypot scandal has inspired some top-notch memes | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The internet is having a field day with Nvidia's Jensen Huang's alleged honeypot scandal.
articles.body_text: Jensen Huang, the CEO and co-founder of the world’s most prominent chip company, has allegedly been honey-trapped by a suspected Chinese spy, and the news has struck the internet like a match to gasoline. Huang has long been seen as a wife guy (or so everyone assumed). He and his wife, Lori, have been together since the 1980s, and both of their children work at Nvidia. Huang has been the closest thing the tech world has to a rock star, with fans lining up for selfies and autographs. Of all the AI overlords, the leather-jacket wearing Huang has seemed like the most level-headed and least erratic, which is why this plot twist has hit so hard. The potential fallout is mind-boggling. Nvidia looms so large over the U.S. stock market that even the company’s domestic drama is a market risk. Countless AI startups depend on Nvidia chips, so any shake-up at the top would ripple far beyond the company. And Nvidia has no publicly disclosed succession plan, so if Huang leaves, it’s unclear who’d take over. Is this how the AI bubble bursts? It’s a question that will be answered in time, but in the meantime, a more pressing matter demands our attention: ranking the funniest memes about the scandal, with bonus points for AI images presumably generated using Nvidia chips. There’s admittedly a lot to choose from, ranging from “500 Days of Summer” jokes to jokes about divorce lawyers to an AI-adaptation of the music video for Usher ‘s song “Confessions Pt. II,” a track about cheating. Another person created a viral AI video that recreates the Coldplay concert where a startup CEO was caught on the Jumbotron hugging a colleague. Huang publicly confessed to the affair just yesterday, so the internet has the rest of the week to get creative. articles.title: A short seller flagged Nvidia CEO's ties to a suspected Chinese spy six months before the scandal | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Six months before Nvidia's spy scandal erupted, Culper Research was already questioning Jensen Huang's unusually close relationship with a Chinese executive.
articles.body_text: Six months before the Nvidia spy scandal emerged , the New York-based short seller firm Culper Research had already raised questions about Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s unusually close relationship with Alice Huang, an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company that buys Nvidia chips. She is now suspected to be a Chinese spy. The Nvidia CEO admitted to an extramarital affair over the weekend, and the company has now opened a formal investigation into his relationship with Alice Huang (who shares his last name but is not related). U.S. intelligence officials believe she was recruited by the Chinese government to collect intelligence on Jensen Huang and influence his position regarding U.S. export controls on advanced AI chips. Culper’s May 13 report is resurfacing because it picked up on the connection between Jensen Huang and Alice Huang while investigating Megaspeed’s ties to Nvidia. NEW: We are short Nvidia $NVDA . We believe Nvidia has a significant China problem. Please see our full report and disclosures now available on our website, link in bio. pic.twitter.com/oTaJyL7S2R In particular, the report called the relationship between the two executives “uncomfortably close,” noting that the Nvidia CEO was spotted partying and socializing with Alice Huang on multiple occasions. The report even claimed that some Nvidia employees wondered whether they had a “special relationship.” Culper Research also theorized the China business that Nvidia lost to export controls had been rerouted through Southeast Asia, and that Megaspeed, a major chip buyer in the region, was secretly financed by Chinese tech giant Alibaba through shell companies. It pointed to financial records that showed Megaspeed’s total liabilities and equity had grown from $33 million at the end of 2023 to around $3 billion by the end of 2024, much of it in the form of refundable deposits from an unidentified source. Financial Times reported Monday that documents show Alibaba lent money to Megaspeed through subsidiaries. Culper is a short seller, so it stood to financially benefit from making these allegations, and those about possible illegal chip diversion have not been independently verified. articles.title: The race is on to sue Nvidia | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Nvidia’s stock slid more than 4% after its board opened an investigation into Jensen Huang’s relationship with a suspected Chinese spy, and one securities law expert says the company’s earlier insistence that it was all “normal” could turn into a very expensive problem.
articles.body_text: Nvidia’s stock slid more than 4% on Monday, the first trading day after its board said it would investigate CEO Jensen Huang over his relationship with Alice Huang, an executive U.S. intelligence believes was spying for China. Securities lawyers were already moving. At least four firms, including Schall, Brown & Schwartz and Levi & Korsinsky, announced investigations Monday into whether Nvidia misled investors. Robert Bartlett, a Stanford Law professor and securities law expert, expects them to have plenty of company. “I would definitely wager that there’ll be a filing,” Bartlett said in an interview Monday morning, adding that he wouldn’t be surprised if a case had been filed by the end of the day. Plaintiffs’ lawyers have good reasons to be first in line; under federal securities law, the first complaint triggers a public notice, and investors then have 60 days to ask the court to be named lead plaintiff. A firm that files early gets a head start on signing up investors with large losses, as well as on shaping the story of the case. Bartlett was right, in fact. A case surfaced Monday afternoon in the Northern District of California, where Nvidia is headquartered. Rosen Law Firm, a New York-based plaintiffs’ firm that specializes in securities class actions, filed it on behalf of Mark Kistenmacher, a retail investor who made seven purchases totaling roughly $20,500 this year, according to a schedule attached to the complaint. (Rosen was lead counsel in a $250 million settlement with Alibaba and ranks among the most active filers of such cases.) The proposed class covers anyone who bought Nvidia securities between Oct. 9, 2025, and Nov. 8, 2026, and the suit names both Nvidia and Huang. The complaint accuses them of misleading investors about Huang’s ties to Megaspeed, the Singapore-based data center outfit where Alice Huang was considered a top exec, and it points to three statements as proof: Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo’s late-October claim that Huang’s interactions with Alice Huang were “not unusual or unexpected,” the company’s even earlier claim that it found “ no evidence of diversion ” of its chips, and Jensen Huang’s Oct. 30 comment to Bloomberg that Nvidia’s dealings with Megaspeed were “ normal and not unusual .” All three were false or misleading, the suit says, because Huang was having an affair with Alice Huang. Kistenmacher is asking for unspecified damages, interest and attorneys’ fees, and he wants a jury trial. While much remains unknown, the legal theory here doesn’t depend on anything the board’s investigation may turn up about Huang’s private life. When The New York Times first reported on Huang’s ties to Alice Huang last month, Rizzo really did tell the Times that the relationship was “ not unusual or unexpected .” Rizzo separately told another outlet , The Hill, that “Megaspeed has been no different than many other regional cloud customers. Meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year.” Of course, the world now knows that was not true. Worse, the Times reports that U.S. intelligence had been monitoring Alice Huang for more than a year. From a securities perspective, Bartlett said, the company’s earlier statement was “clearly a misleading statement.” And because Huang is CEO, Bartlett said, “his knowledge gets imputed to the company.” In other words, Nvidia is treated as having known what its chief executive knew. The Kistenmacher complaint makes the same argument. Bartlett predicted a “classic fraud on the market” claim, in which investors argue they paid prices that reflected false or incomplete public information, and lost money when the truth emerged. This early lawsuit relies on that theory, and Monday’s drop of $7.97 per share, or 4.27%, gives the attorneys involved a lot to work with. Damages in such cases are tied to the stock’s decline, and Nvidia is one of the most valuable companies in the world, so you can imagine a settlement could prove exceedingly expensive. That means a large payment from the company and its directors-and-officers insurers, but typically no personal consequences for the CEO or the board. It is also a civil matter, so Huang isn’t facing prison over it. The irony, as Bartlett noted, is that the suit is brought in the name of Nvidia’s shareholders, and shareholders ultimately pay for the settlement, directly or through insurance premiums.

articles.title: Anthropic releases new Mythos and Fable models amid RSI concerns | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Anthropic says the new models "show improvements in areas like coding, reasoning, and vision," as well as in communicating more clearly with users.
articles.body_text: Anthropic released new versions of its most advanced models on Monday, with the launch of Mythos 5.2 and Fable 5.2. The company says the new models “show improvements in areas like coding, reasoning, and vision” and communicate more clearly with users. Notably, Anthropic is lowering the cost of Fable from $10 to $8 per million input tokens. As a result, Fable 5.2 is now cheaper than its primary competitor GPT-6 Astra. Anthropic says that the new version of Fable will return responses 30% faster across effort levels. Faster inference serving is available for double the price. Fable 5.2 is also compatible with zero data retention (ZDR) policies through the Enterprise Frontier Safeguards system , long a sticking point for many enterprise clients. It’s Anthropic’s first model release since the arrival of a third-party report from the assessment group METR , which suggested the lab might be approaching recursive self-improvement (RSI) — or the ability for AI models to carry on model training independently. The METR report found internal models were speeding up Anthropic’s AI progress by roughly 2x, although many uncertainties remain. Still, Anthropic’s release notes significant ongoing challenges in accurately testing model capabilities. “Claude Mythos 5.2 and Fable 5.2 each voice suspicion that they are being evaluated more often than any of our recent models, which challenges our ability to assess how they will act in real-world settings. As these settings expand and capabilities increase with future models, we expect this challenge to grow.” Anthropic maintains that the new version of Mythos does not have the ability to act covertly against its user, a verdict that’s detailed further in Mythos 5.2’s system card . “Claude Mythos 5.2 shows stronger covert capabilities than prior Claude models on several of our evaluations, particularly when its reasoning is hidden from the monitor,” the system card reads. “That said, we believe that low levels of absolute performance on our new covert evaluations support claims that rely on detection of harmful actions in high-stakes situations.” Fable 5.2 has been available to select parties in pre-release for some time, and Anthropic says the model has already “solved two open problems in theoretical physics, formalized Fermat’s Last Theorem, and supported numerous other research projects.” Also on Monday, AI startup Physical Superintelligence announced a new proof of the Aaronson‑Ambainis conjecture, a pivotal step in setting theoretical limits for quantum computing. Notably, the lab said the result was achieved by running “a non-public Anthropic model” within PSI’s own system. Anthropic did not confirm or deny whether Fable 5.2 was the model in question. articles.title: Jensen Huang’s affair with alleged Chinese spy puts Nvidia’s China ambitions under scrutiny | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Jensen Huang’s alleged affair with a suspected Chinese spy threatens to complicate Nvidia’s lobbying efforts to loosen U.S. chip export restrictions and maintain access to China’s lucrative AI market.
articles.body_text: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has never been quiet about his belief that the U.S. should continue selling AI chips to China, rather than shutting the country off from the technology. The revelation that he had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy threatens to complicate that argument. The Financial Times reported Friday on Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Megaspeed, an Nvidia customer. Jensen Huang admitted to the affair and apologized in a memo to the company on Sunday. U.S. intelligence officials believe Alice Huang was recruited by Chinese intelligence to gather information about the CEO and influence the company’s efforts to loosen chip export restrictions. Nvidia’s independent directors, working with outside legal counsel, are investigating the matter, and Congress is already demanding answers . The controversy comes at a sensitive moment for Nvidia. Historically, China has been a big market for the company. It has shrunk in recent years due to strict U.S. export controls and an aggressive push by Beijing for domestic alternatives. In the three months ended July 26, Nvidia recorded $7.9 billion in revenue from customers headquartered in China, roughly 8% of total revenue. Huang has repeatedly lobbied the U.S. government to expand access to China , and some of his persuasion tactics have been successful. Huang met repeatedly with President Donald Trump and administration officials last year; afterward, the government reversed restrictions on Nvidia’s H20 chips and allowed exports of its more powerful H200 processors. On numerous occasions, Huang has publicly lamented export controls, calling them a “ failure ” at a conference last year and saying in May that it was “ not wise ” for the U.S. and China to create two distinct AI ecosystems. He has also warned that shutting Nvidia out of China’s compute market would enable the country to develop its own AI chips to challenge Nvidia internationally. China is already moving in that direction. Reuters reported last week that about 600,000 H200 chips are being held in Hong Kong, awaiting shipment to mainland China. Beijing is pushing AI companies to prioritize buying chips from Chinese companies instead. The idea that Huang needed any encouragement in the form of an attractive woman to push for greater access to China seems like a stretch, particularly because his lobbying efforts predate their reported meeting at an Nvidia event in early 2024. At the end of the day, Huang is a salesman trying to dominate one of the world’s biggest AI markets. Still, the allegations involving Alice Huang open new scrutiny of the company’s business relationships and could taint any assurances Nvidia offers that it can prevent sensitive technology from reaching unauthorized customers. Once made, rumors of questionable allegiances can be hard to shake. Secretary of State Marco Rubio reportedly warned officials close to Trump earlier this year about Huang’s relationship with an alleged spy. Even if Nvidia’s investigation finds that Huang didn’t share secrets with his paramour, the question is whether he’ll be able to convince Washington that Nvidia can still responsibly do business with China. Nvidia did not respond to a request for comment. When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . This doesn’t affect our editorial independence.

articles.title: Anthropic joins AI’s natural gas frenzy, buys $3.4B worth of turbines | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Anthropic bought billions of dollars' worth of natural gas turbines in a deal that could give it buyer's remorse.
articles.body_text: AI’s power crunch has become so acute that Anthropic, a company that has generally avoided buying physical infrastructure, is spending $3.4 billion on natural gas turbines. The AI company, which is planning to go public this year, is buying Caterpillar generators that equipment supplier OnePWR had originally ordered, according to a Financial Times report . The generators are capable of producing up to 1.7 gigawatts of electricity. Historically, Anthropic has preferred to rent rather than buy. The company disclosed in its S-1 filing in May that it is paying SpaceX subsidiary xAI $1.25 billion per month through May 2029 to use xAI’s computing power. “We expect to enter into additional similar services contracts,” Anthropic stated in the filing, meaning more deals to rent computing power. But as demand for compute ramps up, the market for power has also grown increasingly uncertain, which may have forced its hand. The backlog for natural gas turbines stretches into the early 2030s, and queues to connect to the electrical grid can be just as long. Anthropic’s purchase looks like a last resort. According to the report, OnePWR ordered the turbines a couple years ago but couldn’t find financing to complete the purchase. Anthropic had planned to buy them from OnePWR but instead went directly to Caterpillar, the manufacturer. It’s not clear why OnePWR was unable to secure financing despite Anthropic’s apparent interest as a customer. Whatever the case, Anthropic likely wanted to keep the generating capacity to itself rather than give a competitor an opportunity to snap it up. AI companies have been ramping up their purchases of natural gas equipment and supplies in recent years. Google , Amazon , Microsoft , and Meta have all announced plans to build massive natural gas power plants to power their data centers on-site, rather than drawing from the public grid. The binge has given a second wind to fracking , the drilling method used to extract natural gas from underground rock. And if the buildout proceeds as planned, U.S. data centers alone could consume more natural gas than Germany and Japan combined by 2035. The reliance on natural gas also exposes hyperscalers to price fluctuations. One analyst expects that prices could more than triple by the end of the decade in some markets. If that happens, Anthropic might have a serious case of buyer’s remorse. When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . articles.title: Waymo robotaxis kept illegally passing school buses after software fix, feds say | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The update to Waymo's self-driving system was rolled out nearly a year ago.
articles.body_text: Nearly a year ago, Waymo updated its self-driving software and issued a recall after numerous reports that its robotaxis were illegally passing school buses that had stopped and deployed flashing red lights. Now, federal safety regulators have opened a new investigation into why that behavior has continued. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) said in a November 6 filing that a majority of these reported incidents occurred after the company deployed a software update intended to fix the problem. Reuters was the first to report the filing. Waymo said last year that a software update was completed for all affected vehicles on November 17, 2025. However, NHTSA said the majority of the incidents occurred after the software update. NHTSA’s Office of Defects Investigation (ODI) has opened a “recall query” to “assess the adequacy of the remedy.” The ODI opened its initial investigation into Waymo in October 2025 after seeing footage of one of its autonomous vehicles maneuvering around a stopped school bus that had its stop sign extended, lights flashing, and was unloading children in Atlanta. In that incident, a Waymo robotaxi crossed perpendicularly in front of the school bus from its right side. The autonomous vehicle then turned left around the front of the bus before traveling down the street. Numerous other incidents have been documented in the weeks and months since in Austin, where Waymo also operates a robotaxi service. Austin Independent School District officials reported at least five such incidents at the time, according to a letter filed with NHTSA. Reached for comment, Waymo stressed the importance of safety to its mission. “We have made significant improvements to vehicle behavior around school buses and have received no citations since March 2026,” a spokesperson told TechCrunch via email. “The Waymo Driver has a clearly demonstrated positive impact on roadway safety. Once received, we’ll work to respond to NHTSA’s query and look forward to continuing our engagement on recall processes for AV software that continues to learn and improve.” TechCrunch also reached out to Austin Independent School District officials for comment and will update the article if they respond. articles.title: Is Jensen Huang’s job on the line? Yale’s Jeffrey Sonnenfeld estimates it’s 'about a 50-50' | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Nvidia’s board is investigating Jensen Huang over his relationship with a suspected Chinese spy, and Yale’s Jeffrey Sonnenfeld thinks it’s roughly a coin flip whether Huang stays on as CEO.
articles.body_text: Nvidia’s board announced Sunday that it’s launching an independent investigation after CEO Jensen Huang told staff he was unfaithful to his wife. But this isn’t a case of just another CEO having an extramarital affair. The romantic interest is Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, whom U.S. officials believe is a Chinese spy who was feeding information back to Beijing. In short, the stakes reach well beyond Nvidia, given how many tech and financial partners depend on its place at the center of the AI economy. “I’m responsible for an entire industry ,” Huang recently told Bloomberg in a sit-down. A spokesperson for the Chinese Embassy in Washington dismissed the allegations in late October as “ groundless smears and slanders ,” and no one has been charged. But U.S. intelligence officials reportedly briefed President Donald Trump about their concerns a year ago, and unnamed senior officials inside the Trump administration told the Times that they doubt Huang could have remained unaware all that time of Alice Huang’s intelligence-gathering role for China. When Trump was first briefed, the Times reported, officials didn’t believe Huang knew, and it isn’t clear whether their assessment has changed. The board, meanwhile, says it sees no sign that national security or company secrets were compromised. The question is whether Huang can survive this. To think through what could come next, this editor spoke Sunday with famed professor Jeffrey Sonnenfeld, senior associate dean for leadership studies at the Yale School of Management and founder of the Chief Executive Leadership Institute, which has hosted Huang at its CEO summits. Sonnenfeld likes Huang, he said, and he called Huang’s career salvageable but put the odds at “about a 50-50.” He also had a lot more food for thought. First, the damage. Until now, Huang has been “revered and trusted by everybody in technology,” Sonnenfeld noted. But he called this episode “remarkably poor judgment.” Even if Huang was merely naive, he said, “any employee in Nvidia other than him would be fired over this,” and the recklessness alone would mean “an irretrievable loss of confidence.” Sonnenfeld suggested that Huang’s saving grace could be what social psychologists call idiosyncrasy credits , if he can prove he was being duped. The term comes from Edwin Hollander, a social psychologist who proposed in a 1958 paper that people earn latitude in a group by showing competence and following its rules. Huang has been earning latitude since he co-founded Nvidia in 1993. But all that goodwill can run out when a screw-up looks self-serving or touches the group’s core norms. Here that group includes Nvidia’s board, its roughly 42,000 employees who are bound by security rules, and, in a looser sense, the U.S. government, given it restricts its exports. We also talked about precedents, except, as it turns out, there really are none for what’s unfolding right now. Executives who survive personal scandals sometimes pick up where they left off at another company, Sonnenfeld observed. Former HP CEO Mark Hurd is one example. Between 2005 and 2010, he drove HP to the top of the tech industry by revenue, then was pressured to resign after he filed inaccurate expense reports that hid a personal relationship with a contractor. Oracle hired him about a month later. Huang has no equivalent because Nvidia is his company As for the bench at Nvidia, that doesn’t really exist either. While there is typically a hierarchy inside companies of Nvidia’s scale and importance, Huang has kept things as flat as possible, with about 60 direct reports by his own account. That structure makes it hard to figure out who would succeed him (though his children, both of whom work at Nvidia, are sometimes the subject of succession speculation ). That won’t stop the worldwide guessing game that’s sure to follow. And boards in crisis often reach for a “messianic solution” from outside, Sonnenfeld said, floating former Google CEO Eric Schmidt as one idea. Nvidia’s role at the center of a massive and complex circular financing web is what makes this particular predicament so tricky and, undoubtedly, terrifying for a wide number of constituents. Nvidia isn’t just the biggest provider of chips driving the AI boom but also largely the bank behind the buildout. In addition to stakes in hundreds of smaller startups, Nvidia has invested in OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI, CoreWeave, and Nebius. In August, it also signed preliminary agreements with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, and KKR aimed at mobilizing more than $500 billion over time, and Huang has said Nvidia could backstop up to a quarter of it. The move was widely interpreted as a way to spread risk. Now, a leadership crisis at the center is how a stumble becomes a collapse. So what’s Nvidia’s board likely doing at this moment? Sonnenfeld noted that Huang’s constant, public advocacy for selling advanced chips to China had already made people anxious. Anthropic’s Dario Amodei, whose company Nvidia has backed, had a lot to say about selling chips to China at Davos back in January, likening it to “ selling nuclear weapons to North Korea .” Now the board’s independent members — meaning everyone but Huang — will have to establish what technology reached China if any, and by what routes, including by better understanding Nvidia’s relationship with Megaspeed. The Singapore cloud company, which grew out of a Chinese gaming business and became Nvidia’s largest buyer in Southeast Asia, bought roughly $2 billion of its chips , The New York Times reported in October 2025, raising broader questions about whether it was helping China circumvent U.S. export restrictions by re-exporting the chips to China or renting them to Chinese customers remotely. (An Nvidia spokesperson told The Hill after the Times report that the allegations were “thoroughly investigated and debunked last year .”) In the meantime, Huang will keep running the company, Nvidia said Sunday. That’ll be a tall order, even for a CEO who already spends much of his time traveling the world to promote Nvidia. For starters, three House chairmen want a closed-door briefing from Huang on November 18. Nvidia is also reporting its newest earnings on November 17. Sonnenfeld expects that even if Huang keeps the title, he’ll have to hand off some of the day-to-day decision-making. Only one thing is certain right now. Huang doesn’t own the kind of super-voting stock that would cement his power at Nvidia. Sonnenfeld often argues for dual-class structures that empower founders, and he says Huang’s success without one has been the best counterargument to that case. But if Huang had one, Sonnenfeld continued, removing him would be harder.

articles.title: 3D DRAM created by IBM and Micron, 128GBps memory on the way
articles.summary: Smaller and faster RAM with up to 128GB transfer speed scould be on the way thanks to research from IBM and MIcron, using stacked chips and TSVs.
articles.body_text: Smaller and faster RAM with up to 128GBps transfer speeds could be on the way thanks to research from IBM and MIcron. The companies have developed three-dimensional memory, stacking individual DRAM chips vertically that would normally have to be placed side-by-side, though the efficiencies gained aren’t solely down to space. Communication between the stacked chips and the host device is achieved through a new creation known as through-silicon vias, or TSVs, which run vertically through the pile of chips and act as conduits to the host device. Thanks to the TSVs, in testing the memory has reached data speeds of 128GBps, ten times faster than current memory. On top of this, IBM claims the chips are 70 percent more power efficient than today’s DRAM. The new research is expected to form a key part of Samsung and Micron’s Hybrid Memory Cube technology, first announced back in October. IBM and Micron hope to have commercial availability in two years, with servers likely to use it first. Looking beyond that, IBM fellow Subu Iyer said that the new process “will have applications beyond memory, enabling other industry segments as well.” What exactly those new segments are remains to be seen, but we certainly wouldn’t complain if our computers got the kind of speed bump described here.

articles.summary: En pappa och hans två unga söner sålde tusentals förfalskade Apple-klockor och hörlurar som liknar airpods. Nu döms trion för ett ”gemensamt brottsprojekt”. Pappan ska också betala nästan 2,7 miljoner kronor i skadestånd.
articles.body_text: En pappa och hans två unga söner sålde tusentals förfalskade Apple-klockor och hörlurar som liknar airpods. Nu döms trion för ett ”gemensamt brottsprojekt”. Pappan ska också betala nästan 2,7 miljoner kronor i skadestånd. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Utredningen påbörjades i slutet av 2023. Då hade den svenska tullen stoppat en leverans med misstänkt förfalskade airpods, och när Apple sen kunde konstatera att produkterna inte var äkta gjordes en polisanmälan. I maj i år åtalades en pappa i 60-årsåldern och hans två söner, båda i 20-årsåldern och från Stockholmsområdet, för att ha importerat förfalskade hörlurar och klockor, näst intill identiska med Apples varianter, och sen marknadsfört dem genom att använda Apples olika varumärken, som airpods, earpods och Apple watch. Enligt polisen sålde de minst 4 000 kopior och gjorde en vinst på 3,3 miljoner kronor. Nu har alla tre dömts för grovt varumärkesbrott och grovt mönsterskyddsbrott under perioden oktober 2023–juli 2025. ■ Mönsterrätt är ett immaterialrättsligt skydd som är till för att skydda nya designer, mönster och former. Enligt polis och åklagare har pappan och sönerna i det här fallet använt sig av ”mönster som varit identiska” med Apples. Pappan har erkänt de faktiska omständigheterna men menar att han enbart hade en mindre roll i verksamheten och inte visste att det han gjorde var olagligt. – I min värld, det jag och dom gör, ingen blåser någon. Den enda som är besviken är Apple. De är miljardärer, har han sagt i polisförhör. Sönerna har uppgett att de vid några tillfällen hjälpt sin pappa med marknadsföring och översättning, men de har förnekat brott.

articles.title: USA vill se ”slutgiltigt slut” på kriget – samtal inleds
articles.summary: Ryssland, Ukraina och USA möts i Abu Dhabi.
articles.body_text: Ryssland, Ukraina och USA möts i Abu Dhabi. Det är de första substantiella förhandlingarna mellan de två länderna sedan i början av året. På bordet finns en ny ”långsiktig säkerhetsarkitektur”, ett återupplivande av Nato-Ryssland-rådet och eventuellt hävda sanktioner mot Ryssland, rapporterar The Guardian . Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. USA vill se ett ”slutgiltigt slut” på kriget och tycks inför samtalen vara villiga till stora eftergifter till Ryssland för att få till ett avtal. Ukrainas president Volodymyr Zelenskyj står fast vid att han inte vill ge upp något territorium till Ryssland. På tisdagen sätter sig Ryssland och Ukraina ner för att återuppta de samtal som brakade ihop i februari. Med på mötet finns också USA och i kulisserna även Europa. Amerikanska företrädare säger att deras avsikt är att verka för ett ”slutgiltigt slut” på kriget och enligt företrädare för Trump-administrationen kommer man att försöka utforma en ny ”långsiktig säkerhetsarkitektur” mellan Ryssland och Europa, rapporterar The Guardian. För Ryssland har det enda sedan Vladimir Putin kom till makten varit prioriterat att omförhandla maktbalansen mellan Nato och Ryssland. Att en amerikansk sittande president accepterar att de kraven omfattas beskrivs av tidningen som ett tecken på den desperata viljan från amerikanskt håll att nå en överenskommelse. Ukraina och Ryssland sätter sig ner vid förhandlingsbordet igen – första gången på nio månader. Samtal förs i två dagar i Förenade arabemiratens huvudstad Abu Dhabi och med vid bordet sitter USA. Ukraina och USA möter under dagarna också representanter för Tyskland, Frankrike, Storbritannien och Italien, samt Nato och Europeiska unionen.

articles.body_text: S-ledaren Magdalena Andersson riktar nu udden mot Centerpartiet i regeringsbildningskaoset. Nu uppmanar hon partiet att ge förslag om hur V ska kunna få inflytande i en rödgrön regering. – Centerpartiet behöver naturligtvis också bjuda till, säger hon i SVT:s ”Morgonstudion” . Under tisdagsmorgonen gästar Magdalena Andersson Morgonstudion och hennes udd tycks nu snarare vara riktad mot Centerpartiets agerande än Vänsterpartiets. Hon tror fortfarande på sin plan om en S-styrd regering med C och MP där V agerar stödparti. – För det här är ju en möjlighet för Centerpartiet att kunna leva upp till båda sina röda linjer, leva upp till de löften som man gav väljarna samtidigt som Vänsterpartiet kan göra avtryck i svensk politik och att alla som har röstat på dem kan få utdelning, säger Andersson. Alternativet, att vara med och bilda en borgerlig minoritetsregering som skulle kräva att beslut är förankrade hos SD, vore förödande för C, enligt Andersson. – Men det är klart, om Centerpartiet skulle välja att göra sig beroende av Sverigedemokraterna, då vore det ett sånt enormt svek. Hon menar även att ett sådant drag från C ”vore det största sveket någonsin i svensk politik”. Samtidigt har 55 dagar gått sen valet och vi har ingen regering. Det är upp till varje parti att fatta beslut om, men då hade man ljugit svenska folket rakt upp i ansiktet. Så många av sina väljare, säger Magdalena Andersson.

articles.body_text: Vladimir Putin har kallat Elon Musk för ”ett geni”. Nu bygger Ryssland ett eget Starlink – som kommer möjliggöra mer effektiva drönarattacker mot mål på längre avstånd. – Det finns potentiella användningsområden för terrorism och sabotage, säger militärexperten Rob Lee till Financial Times. Rysslands president Vladimir Putin hyllade i förra veckan SpaceX-grundaren Elon Musk som ”ett geni” och sa att han står ”i nära kontakt” med honom. SpaceX har utvecklat det satellitbaserade internetsystemet Starlink, vars militära version används av den ukrainska försvarsmakten och möjliggör mycket effektiva drönarattacker. Ryssland arbetar nu mycket intensivt med att bygga ett eget Starlink – Rassvet – som man hoppas ska kunna ta i drift nästa år, rapporterar Financial Times. Det är dåliga nyheter för Ukraina och Europa. Det ryska satellitnätverket skulle underlätta för dataöverföring, styrning av drönare i realtid över långa avstånd och attacker mot rörliga mål, skriver tidningen. – Den största faran ligger inte bara i att Ryssland får ett alternativ till Starlink, utan i att relativt billiga attackdrönare kan förvandlas till vapen som kan identifiera, följa och bekämpa rörliga mål långt inne på ukrainskt territorium, säger Oleksandr Danylyuk, på tankesmedjan Center for Defense Reforms till tidningen. – Med Rysslands snabbt växande drönarproduktion skulle detta avsevärt kunna öka effektiviteten i landets attacker och försvaga Ukrainas förmåga att skydda kritisk militär och civil infrastruktur. Utbyggnaden av Rassvet innebär också säkerhetsrisker för Europa, eftersom drönare kan styras var som helst inom systemets täckningsområde.

articles.title: Chef krävde sex av städare – ska betala skadestånd

articles.body_text: Chefen visade sin penis och hotade med utebliven lön om den kvinnliga städaren inte hade sex med honom. Nu har hon stämt sin chef – som nu ska betala henne flera hundra tusen. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Det hände flera gånger att mannen närmade sig kvinnan sexuellt, rapporterar tidningen Arbetet . En gång ska han ha dragit fram sin penis och sagt att hon skulle ”massera” den. En annan gång gjorde han samma sak igen, mitt under ett städjobb, samtidigt som han höll fast henne. De hade jobbat tillsammans tidigare, innan mannen startade eget bolag. Även då hade han betett sig illa mot kvinna, bland annat genom att slå henne på rumpan och skickat en video där han onanerade. När mannen erbjöd kvinnan jobb i sitt nystartade bolag tackade hon ja, men krävde att hans sexuella trakasserier skulle upphöra. Han sa ja. Bara veckor senare hände det igen och när kvinnan skulle få sin första lön kom det inga pengar. Enligt Arbetet ska mannen ha skyllt den uteblivna lönen på sin revisor, men efter flera månader utan lön kom han med ett nytt svar: Det blir ingen lön om hon inte har sex med honom. Dessutom skulle ingen tro henne om hon anmälde honom eftersom hon var asylsökande, sa han. Hon anmälde honom efter tre månader när hon slutade jobbet, men polisanmälan ledde inte till åtal eftersom brott inte kunde styrkas. Däremot prövade tingsrätten kvinnans krav på skadestånd. I domstolen nekade chefen till brott. Han menade att hon slutade frivilligt för att hon stulit äpplen hos en kund. Rätten bedömde kvinnans version som mer trovärdig, medan chefens version uppfattades som både ”betydligt mer knapphändig” och delvis ”ologisk”. Chefen ska betala nära 390 000 kronor i ersättning till kvinnan, men han ska också betala hennes rättegångskostnader om 468 000 kronor. Domstolen menar att chefen har utsatt kvinnan för sexuella trakasserier och att han inte har betalat ut lön i tid. Rätten menar vidare att det räknas som ett olagligt avskedande när kvinnan slutade jobbet efter att hon i praktiken tvingats därifrån.

Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Socialdemokraternas Magdalena Andersson sa i går att hon vill ha en regering med C, MP och V som stödpart. Det har Vänsterpartiet tidigare sagt absolut nej till, med hänvisning till partiets kongressbeslut om ministerkrav. Men i SVT:s ”Aktuellt” säger nu Gabrielsson att V var redo att förhandla om det mesta med de andra rödgröna partierna – kanske till och med ministerposter. – Det hade vi behövt diskutera ordentligt, säger hon. Hon understryker dock att det skulle bli svårt att backa på den frågan, med anledning av just kongressbeslutet. Gabrielsson tror att C försöker pressa dem genom att samtala med högersidan och att processen partierna befinner sig i nu är ”riggad”. – Jag tror att Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist vill gå över till Åkesson (SD). I de samtal jag har fört har jag varit tydlig med att jag vill hitta en väg, säger hon. Hon beskriver det som att hon blivit lurad och hävdar att C-ledaren aldrig lyft högersidan som ett alternativ i deras samtal. Efter intervjun fortsätter Gabrielsson på X. Hon skriver att C-ledaren, Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist, hade kunnat fortsätta samtalen med de rödgröna partierna ”och hittat vägar framåt”.

articles.body_text: Socialdemokraterna och Moderaterna borde bilda regering tillsammans. Det tycker tidigare S-ministern Thomas Bodström som vill att partiledarna ska dela på statsministerposten. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Under söndagskvällen berättade Magdalena Andersson under en pressträff att hon önskar sig en regering bestående av socialdemokrater, miljöpartister och centerpartister – Vänsterpartiet lämnas utanför. Thomas Bodström , före detta socialdemokratisk justitieminister, hoppas på ett helt annat alternativ. – Det är faktiskt en annan tanke jag haft: Att Socialdemokraterna och Moderaterna skulle kunna bilda en regering med var sitt parti på var sin sida. Då får de en stabil majoritet. För att tillfredsställa bägge partier föreslår han att partierna delar på statsministerposten – två år var. – De kan köra två år var, med var sitt parti. – Ja, det kan man förstås komma överens om. – Socialdemokraterna och Moderaterna, de två största, borde verkligen nu ta ansvar och kliva fram. Jimmie Åkesson har tidigare berättat att Sverigedemokraterna kommer att tolerera Ulf Kristersson som statsminister, utan krav på ministerposter. Talmannen har nu förlängt moderatledarens sonderingsuppdrag. Nu har Centerpartiet ställts inför ett vägval. Enligt Expressens uppgifter tillhör Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist falangen som vill gå högerut och ”läka ihop gamla Alliansen”.

articles.body_text: President Volodymyr Zelenskyj träffar stats- och regeringschefer från de nordiska länderna i Danmark i dag, uppger danska regeringen i ett pressmeddelande. Mötet mellan statsminister Ulf Kristersson (M) och de andra regeringsledarna äger alltså rum samtidigt som fredsförhandlingarna mellan Ryssland, Ukraina och USA i Abu Dhabi, Förenade arabemiraten startar i dag. – Jag är stolt över att kunna välkomna president Zelenskyj och de nordiska ledarna till Danmark. Ukrainarnas kamp för ett fritt Ukraina och ett fritt Europa fortsätter. Deras otroliga mod och deras styrka är en ljuspunkt i en allvarlig och osäker tid, säger statsminister Mette Frederiksen i pressmeddelandet. – Samtidigt är den ryska grymheten ändlös. Snart fem år efter fullskaliga invasionen fortsätter bombregnet riktat mot civila, mot hjälpcenter och mot vatten- och värmeverk. Därför måste vi stå fast. Vi ska fortsätta stödet, och vi ska lära av Ukrainas erfarenheter och kunskap, så att vi tillsammans kan skydda Europa, säger Mette Frederiksen. Tre polisbilar har under tisdagsmorgonen varit på plats vid kommunhuset i Kungälv. Enligt polisen rör det sig om en del av en planerad insats. – Det är inget pågående våldsbrott, säger polisens presstalesperson Jens Andersson. Polisen har varit på plats "under morgontimmarna". Man bekräftar också att det finns en formell misstanke om brott i utredningen. – Ja, det gör det ju. Men det är en fråga för förundersökningsledaren. Just nu är det här det vi kommunicerar, säger Jens Andersson. Under eftermiddagen och kvällen, mellan klockan 15 och 22, kommer polisen tillsammans med räddningstjänsten i Storgöteborg, ambulans och krognäring att genomföra en stor övning på Kungsportsavenyn i centrala Göteborg. Övningen ska gälla en "större allvarlig händelse" med ett "större skadeutfall". Övningen kommer innebära begränsningar i framkomligheten och ett område vid Stadsbiblioteket kommer vara avspärrat, meddelar polisen. En olycka med en lastbil på E4 vid trafikplats Järva krog i norra Stockholm har orsakat stor trafikpåverkan under tisdagsmorgonen, enligt Trafikverket.
